I have farmed this land a long time, and I do not like taking unnecessary risks. On 12 mu, I will keep the main part of the farm in the wheat-maize system because that is what fits my land, my irrigation, and my experience best, and it gives me stable grain output. I will put 8 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 8 mu, and I will keep 4 mu in cotton because cotton still gives me a cash crop and spreads my risk. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters because I want stable emergence, stronger resistance, and better yield, but I will not push fertilizer to extremes because that raises cost without always giving me more grain. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate at the key stages rather than depend only on rain. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale and easier for me to manage across the season. I will spray when needed to protect the crop, but I will keep it to the number of applications I think is enough for normal pressure in my area. My goal is not the highest possible yield on paper; it is a steady harvest I can actually bring in with my household labor and experience.
